title: Nuclear Bombs Revealed the True Age of Your Cells
description:
Cold War nuclear bomb tests left a radioactive fingerprint in every living thing on Earth -- and decades later, scientists turned it into a way to literally date individual cells inside your body. Here's what they found.

#shorts #sciencefacts #biology #didyouknow

scenes.text: In the 1950s and 60s, nuclear bomb tests left a fingerprint inside every human cell on Earth -- one scientists later learned to read.
Those tests roughly doubled the carbon-14 in Earth's atmosphere. Plants absorbed it, we ate the plants, and it got built into every new cell your body has made since.
Decades later, researchers at Sweden's Karolinska Institute realized that same carbon signature could tell them exactly when a specific cell in a living person was made.
Heart muscle cells, it turns out, get replaced at about one percent a year in your twenties, dropping to under half a percent by your seventies.
Fat cells turn over roughly ten times faster -- about one in ten dies and gets replaced every single year, whether you're lean or overweight.
But when they dated neurons in the brain's outer layer, the carbon signature matched almost exactly to the year the person was born. Those cells are never replaced at all.
If a lab could carbon-date any part of your body right now, which part do you think would come back the oldest?
